paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “Today increasing importance is being attached to cultivating college students’ team spirit.” You can make statements, give reasons, or cite examples to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：对于这一部分，你有30分钟的时间写一篇文章，开头是“今天越来越重视培养大学生的团队精神”。你可以发表陈述、给出理由或引用例子来展开你的论文。你应该写至少150字但不超过200字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: American colleges and universities are using 64 percent less coal than they did a decade ago, burning 700,000 tons last year, down from 2 million tons in 2008, the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) said in a report 26 yesterday.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国能源信息署 (EIA) 在昨天发布的一份报告中称，美国高校的煤炭使用量比十年前减少了 64%，去年燃烧了 70 万吨，低于 2008 年的 200 万吨。

paragraphs.sourceText: All 57 schools that were burning coal in 2008 are using less now, and 20 have 27 coal completely, EIA found.
paragraphs.translationZh: EIA 发现，2008 年使用煤炭的所有 57 所学校现在都在减少使用煤炭，其中 20 所学校已经完全放弃煤炭。

paragraphs.sourceText: Most universities have turned to natural gas as a 28 ,with state funding backing the fuel switch.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大多数大学已转向天然气作为替代品，国家资金支持燃料转换。

paragraphs.sourceText: While academic institutions use less than 0.1 percent of U.S. coal burned for power, campus coal use has a history dating back to the 1800s when 29 to power was scarce.
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然学术机构使用的煤炭发电量不到美国的 0.1%，但校园煤炭的使用历史可以追溯到 1800 年代，当时电力匮乏。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many universities still operate their own power plants. The Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 encouraged more electricity generation by allowing institutions to sell 30 power to utilities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多大学仍然经营自己的发电厂。 1978 年的《公用事业监管政策法案》允许机构向公用事业公司出售剩余电力，从而鼓励更多发电。

paragraphs.sourceText: But EIA noted many coal-fired universities have signed onto the American College and University Presidents Climate Commitment, which was launched in 2007.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但 EIA 指出，许多燃煤大学已经签署了 2007 年推出的美国学院和大学校长气候承诺。

paragraphs.sourceText: About 665 schools are part of the program, which aims to 31 greenhouse gas emissions. Thirty percent of the participants have pledged to be carbon 32 within 20 years.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大约 665 所学校参与了该计划，旨在减少温室气体排放。百分之三十的参与者承诺在 20 年内实现碳中和。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Sierra Club’s Beyond Coal campaign, which also leads campaigns for universities to withdraw their 33 in coal and other fossil fuels, lists 22 schools that have pledged to move “beyond coal,” including Clemson University, Indiana University, Ohio University, Penn State University, the University of Louisville and the University of Tennessee, Knoxville.
paragraphs.translationZh: 塞拉俱乐部的“超越煤炭”运动还领导了大学撤回对煤炭和其他化石燃料的投资的运动，该运动列出了 22 所承诺“超越煤炭”的学校，包括克莱姆森大学、印第安纳大学、俄亥俄大学、宾夕法尼亚州立大学、路易斯维尔大学和田纳西大学诺克斯维尔分校。

paragraphs.sourceText: The largest coal use 34 at colleges were in Michigan, Missouri, Tennessee and Indiana. Indiana’s universities alone cut coal 35 by 81 percent between 2008 and 2015.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大学煤炭使用量减少幅度最大的是密歇根州、密苏里州、田纳西州和印第安纳州。 2008 年至 2015 年间，仅印第安纳州的大学就将煤炭消耗量减少了 81%。

paragraphs.sourceText: During the same period, Michigan made an 80 percent cut and Tennessee cut back by 94 percent at state institutions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 同一时期，密歇根州削减了 80%，田纳西州削减了 94%。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Classical music aims to evolve, build audiences without alienating old guard
paragraphs.translationZh: 古典音乐的目标是在不疏远守旧派的情况下发展、吸引观众

paragraphs.sourceText: A) In 1913, classical music sparked a riot in Paris. Igor Stravinsky was introducing his revolutionary “Rite of Spring” ballet to the world, with its discordant melodies and unorthodox choreography (编舞)，and the purists in the crowd expressed their disapproval loud and clear. It might have been classical music’s version of the time Bob Dylan went electric at the Newport Folk Festival. “The noise, fighting, and shouting in the audience got so loud,” NPR’s music reporter Miles Hoffman said of the Stravinsky debut, “that the choreographer had to shout out the numbers to the dancers so that they knew what they were supposed to do.”
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 1913年，古典音乐在巴黎引发骚乱。伊戈尔·斯特拉文斯基正在向世界介绍他革命性的芭蕾舞剧《春之祭》，其不和谐的旋律和非正统的编舞，人群中的纯粹主义者大声而明确地表达了他们的反对。这可能是鲍勃·迪伦在纽波特民谣音乐节上使用电子音乐时的古典音乐版本。 “观众席上的噪音、打斗和喊叫声如此之大，”NPR 的音乐记者迈尔斯·霍夫曼在谈到斯特拉文斯基的首演时说道，“编舞者必须向舞者大声喊出数字，以便他们知道自己应该做什么。”

paragraphs.sourceText: B) It’s difficult to imagine a similar disturbance occurring today within America’s sacred symphony halls. In fact, it’s hard to picture any kind of disruptive activity at all (unless someone’s cell phone happens to go off, and then you’d better watch your back). A mannerly aura (氛围) hangs over most classical proceedings, and many of the genre’s biggest supporters would have it no other way.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 很难想象今天在美国神圣的交响乐厅内会发生类似的骚乱。事实上，很难想象任何类型的破坏性活动（除非某人的手机碰巧响了，然后你最好小心你的背后）。大多数古典乐曲都笼罩着一种彬彬有礼的气氛，许多该流派的最大支持者也别无选择。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Today, Western audiences for classical music and opera and ballet are almost always well dressed, older, respectful, achingly silent and often very wealthy (one has to be able to afford most tickets). But as many of America’s most storied “highbrow” (高雅的) institutions struggle financially — the Philadelphia Orchestra’s much-publicized rebound from bankruptcy is just one recent example — classical music fans and theorists are wondering how the medium can weave itself into the 21st century’s cultural fabric without sacrificing its integrity.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 如今，古典音乐、歌剧和芭蕾舞的西方观众几乎总是衣着考究、年长、有礼貌、沉默寡言，而且往往非常富有（必须有能力买得起大部分门票）。但随着美国许多最著名的“高雅”机构陷入财务困境——广为人知的费城交响乐团从破产中恢复过来只是最近的一个例子——古典音乐迷和理论家们想知道这种媒介如何能够在不牺牲其完整性的情况下融入21世纪的文化结构。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) For example, should we feel OK “clapping” during classical music events, even if nobody else is? Why shouldn’t we cheer for something great, like we do at a rock concert? The Huffington Post recently ran a Great Debate on this issue and many commenters came out on the side of silence. “There is no more rewarding experience in life than being part of an audience where everybody is leaning forward in silence, thoroughly carried away by a great performance of a masterpiece,” one commenter wrote. “Why is it so difficult for folks to develop an appreciation and understanding for the mannerisms and traditions of classical music?” asked another.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 例如，在古典音乐活动期间，我们应该感觉“鼓掌”吗？即使没有其他人这样做？为什么我们不应该为伟大的事情欢呼，就像在摇滚音乐会上那样？ 《赫芬顿邮报》最近就这个问题进行了一场大辩论，许多评论者都站在沉默一边。一位评论者写道：“生活中没有比成为观众中的一员更有价值的经历了，每个人都默默地向前倾身，完全被杰作的精彩表演所陶醉。” “为什么人们很难欣赏和理解古典音乐的风格和传统？”另一个人问道。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) The truth is that classical music audiences weren’t always so polite. Robert Greenberg, an award-winning composer, said that when Beethoven first performed his 7th Symphony, audiences forced the orchestra to perform encores (重演) of certain movements immediately, applauding wildly. And in the last few decades, he said, many audiences at opera performances have abandoned pretenses, yelling “Bravo” when they feel like it.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 事实上，古典音乐观众并不总是那么有礼貌。屡获殊荣的作曲家罗伯特·格林伯格表示，贝多芬第一次演奏《第七交响曲》时，观众立即迫使乐团重演某些乐章，并热烈鼓掌。他说，在过去的几十年里，许多歌剧表演的观众已经放弃了伪装，当他们想喊“好极了”时。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) “I don’t think there’s anything wrong with an audience showing their enthusiasm for a proper moment by applauding, showing their joy,” Greenberg said, noting that the stuffiness in concert halls is “one aspect of contemporary concert etiquette” he doesn’t understand. “Instead of waiting half an hour to show enthusiasm, why not show it every eight or nine minutes?”
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 格林伯格说：“我认为观众在适当的时刻通过鼓掌、表达他们的喜悦来表达他们的热情并没有什么问题。”他指出，音乐厅里的沉闷是他不理解的“当代音乐会礼仪的一个方面”。 “与其等半个小时来表现热情，为什么不每隔八九分钟表现一次呢？”

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Until the rules about behavior and clothing change, it’s hard to imagine multitudes of young people filling concert halls on their own accord. They’re probably more likely to head to Central Park to watch a free performance with a bottle of wine and their friends. “I think anyone should be able to come into a performance dressed any way they like, and be comfortable any way they like, sitting in that seat ready to enjoy themselves,” Greenberg said. “Because it’s enjoyable.”
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 在有关行为和着装的规则发生变化之前，很难想象会有大量年轻人自愿挤满音乐厅。他们可能更有可能带着一瓶酒和朋友去中央公园观看免费表演。格林伯格说：“我认为任何人都应该能够以任何他们喜欢的方式穿着，以任何他们喜欢的方式舒适地坐在那个座位上，准备好享受表演。” “因为这很有趣。”

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Greenberg stressed that he doesn’t want people to start respecting the music less, and he’s not suggesting that we “dumb down” the experience. Rather, it’s about opening up “access.” When operas first instituted subtitles (字幕) during shows, he said, many purists didn’t like the idea, believing that the audience should instead study the works before attending. But now it’s commonplace to find titles on the seatback in front of you — choose a language, sit back, and understand what’s going on.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 格林伯格强调，他不希望人们开始减少对音乐的尊重，他并不是建议我们“简化”这种体验。相反，它是关于开放“访问”。他说，当歌剧首次在演出时设置字幕时，许多纯粹主义者不喜欢这个主意，认为观众应该在观看之前研究一下作品。但现在在你面前的座椅靠背上找到标题已经很常见了——选择一种语言，坐下来，然后了解发生了什么。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Allison Vulgamore, president of the Philadelphia Orchestra, is certainly looking to the future. She says certain “classics concerts” dedicated to the old masters will always exist, but not every program has to feature Beethoven and Brahms — or even a stage and seats. “We’re trying to introduce different kinds of concerts in different ways,” she said. “We are an interactive society now, where people like to learn.”
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 费城交响乐团团长艾莉森·沃尔加莫尔 (Allison Vulgamore) 无疑正在展望未来。她说，某些献给古代大师的“经典音乐会”将永远存在，但并不是每个节目都必须以贝多芬和勃拉姆斯为特色，甚至不需要舞台和座位。 “我们正在尝试以不同的方式推出不同类型的音乐会，”她说。 “我们现在是一个互动社会，人们喜欢学习。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J) As the Philadelphia Orchestra rebounds from its financial straits, it is also aiming to experiment, without alienating the loyalists. Vulgamore pointed to Cirque de la Symphonie, a recent offering in which jugglers (玩杂耍的人) and acrobats (杂技演员) interacted with musicians. An upcoming collaboration with New York City’s Ridge Theatre, meanwhile, will feature a “suspended dance installation” and other theatrical elements occurring in conjunction with an orchestral piece.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 随着费城交响乐团从财务困境中恢复过来，它也打算在不疏远忠实拥护者的情况下进行实验。 Vulgamore 提到了 Cirque de la Symphonie，这是最近推出的一项节目，杂技演员和杂技演员与音乐家互动。与此同时，即将与纽约市里奇剧院合作，将以“悬浮舞蹈装置”和其他与管弦乐作品结合的戏剧元素为特色。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) The orchestra also continues to offer $25 annual memberships to Philadelphia students, who can buy rush tickets to every concert on the schedule. “Students line up for the concerts they want, and we get roughly 300 or 350 kids a night coming to these. They take any of the open seats available, 5 minutes before the concert starts,” Vulgamore said. “It’s like the running of the bulls, that energy when the doors open.”
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 乐团还继续向费城学生提供 25 美元的年度会员资格，他们可以购买时间表上每场音乐会的抢票。 “学生们排队观看他们想要的音乐会，每晚大约有 300 或 350 名孩子来观看这些音乐会。他们会在音乐会开始前 5 分钟占据任何空位，”Vulgamore 说。 “这就像公牛奔跑一样，当大门打开时就会充满能量。”

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Greenberg thinks that youthful energy needs to be harvested. Conductors don’t have to be arrogant and untouchable — they can be accessible. Perhaps there could even be a “bit of humor” about them, he suggested, and an abandoning of pretension within the high-art institutions themselves. “On one hand, these organizations are all saying the same thing: we want more general audiences, to break down cultural barriers,” he said. “But then they come up with some very snooty (目中无人的) thing that makes you crazy.”
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 格林伯格认为年轻的能量需要收获。指挥不必傲慢无礼、高不可攀——他们可以平易近人。他建议，也许他们甚至可以有一点“幽默感”，并且放弃高雅艺术机构内部的自命不凡。 “一方面，这些组织都在说同样的事情：我们想要更多的普通受众，以打破文化障碍，”他说。 “但后来他们想出了一些非常傲慢的东西，让你发疯。”

paragraphs.sourceText: M) John Terauds, a critic who has covered Toronto’s classical music scene extensively, also wants to do away with the stuffiness. He suggested that the warmer an audience is, the better the musicians themselves will respond. “But the producer or organizer has to let everyone know it’s OK,” he said. “It’s OK to enjoy yourself.” At the Toronto Symphony Orchestra, for example, conductor Peter Oundjian often stops between pieces, taking a moment to talk about the composer or the music in a very amiable way. And some nights, Terauds said, “at least a third” of the audience consists of students who have purchased cheaper tickets. On these nights, the energy of the room drastically shifts. It becomes a less intimidating place.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) John Terauds 是一位广泛报道多伦多古典音乐界的评论家，他也希望消除这种乏味。他建议观众越热情，音乐家自己的反应就越好。 “但制片人或组织者必须让每个人都知道这是可以的，”他说。 “玩得开心就可以了。”例如，在多伦多交响乐团，指挥家彼得·奥德吉安经常在乐曲之间停下来，花点时间以一种非常和蔼可亲的方式谈论作曲家或音乐。特劳兹说，有些晚上，“至少三分之一”的观众是购买更便宜门票的学生。在这些夜晚，房间里的能量发生了巨大的变化。它变成了一个不那么令人生畏的地方。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Back in February, Terauds wrote on his blog about how going to classical performances can be intimidating. Certain people “think they have to dress up,” he wrote. “They think they have to know something about the music before they go. And, I’m sure, sitting in a seat, trembling in fear that this might be the wrong time to applaud, is also one of the factors.”
paragraphs.translationZh: N）早在二月份，Terauds 在他的博客上写道，去看古典表演可能会让人感到害怕。他写道，某些人“认为他们必须打扮得漂漂亮亮”。 “他们认为在走之前必须对音乐有所了解。而且，我确信，坐在座位上，担心这可能是错误的鼓掌时间而颤抖，也是因素之一。”

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Everyone in the classical world agrees on the need for increased “accessibility,” but achieving it is often easier said than done. Nowadays, there are unknown, unorthodox opera singers wowing (博得……的喝彩) viewers on TV programs like “America’s Got Talent” and “The Voice”. What can higher institutions do with any of that? And if they appeal to these outlets, do they risk compromising the integrity or the intelligence of the music?
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 古典世界中的每个人都同意需要增加“可访问性”，但实现这一点往往说起来容易做起来难。如今，在《美国达人秀》、《美国好声音》等电视节目中，有一些默默无闻、非正统的歌剧歌手让观众惊叹不已。高等院校可以利用这些做什么呢？如果他们吸引这些渠道，他们是否会冒着损害音乐完整性或智慧的风险？

paragraphs.sourceText: P. Vulgamore seems to understand this. She thinks an organization can have it both ways, claiming the new while keeping the old. And as she reorganizes the Philadelphia Orchestra, she will attempt to do just that. “The world’s most respected musicians brought together as an orchestra will always exist,” she said. “But it’s essential that we be willing to experiment and fail.”
paragraphs.translationZh: P. Vulgamore 似乎明白这一点。她认为一个组织可以双管齐下，既求新又保留旧的。当她重组费城交响乐团时，她将尝试这样做。 “世界上最受尊敬的音乐家聚集在一起组成一个管弦乐队将永远存在，”她说。 “但我们必须愿意尝试并接受失败，这一点至关重要。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. It was not a rare occurrence that audiences behaved wildly while listening to classical music.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 观众在听古典音乐时表现得很疯狂的情况并不少见。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Some high-art institutions don’t actually mean it when they say they want more general audiences.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 一些高雅艺术机构说他们想要更多的普通观众，但他们实际上并不是真心的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. The theatre was in chaos when an unconventional ballet was first put on stage in the capital of France.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 当一部非常规芭蕾舞剧首次在法国首都上演时，剧院一片混乱。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. According to one critic, the audience’s warm response would encourage the musicians to do a better job.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 据一位评论家说，观众的热烈反应会鼓励音乐家做得更好。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Many commenters argued for the audience enjoying classical music quietly.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 许多评论者主张观众安静地欣赏古典音乐。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. What appears on the seatback screen makes it unnecessary for the audience to study the works beforehand.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 座椅靠背屏幕上出现的内容使得观众无需事先研究作品。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. It is generally accepted that there should be no disturbance from the audience during classical music performance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 人们普遍认为，古典音乐表演期间不应干扰观众。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Higher institutions will be concerned about compromising the integrity of classical music if they have to resort to the television medium.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 高等院校如果不得不诉诸电视媒体，将会担心古典音乐的完整性受到损害。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Heavily discounted rush tickets help attract many young students to attend classical concerts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 大幅折扣的抢购票吸引了许多年轻学生来观看古典音乐会。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. The formalities of high-art theatres can intimidate some people attending a performance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 高级艺术剧院的拘谨可能会吓到一些观看表演的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: How can one person enjoy good health, while another person looks old before her time? Humans have been asking this question for thousands of years, and recently, it’s becoming clearer and clearer to scientists that the differences between people’s rates of aging lie in the complex interactions among genes, social relationships, environments and lifestyles. Even though you were born with a particular set of genes, the way you live can influence how they express themselves. Some lifestyle factors may even turn genes on or shut them off.
paragraphs.translationZh: 怎么可能一个人身体健康，而另一个人却过早衰老呢？几千年来，人类一直在问这个问题，最近，科学家们越来越清楚地认识到，人们衰老速度的差异在于基因、社会关系、环境和生活方式之间复杂的相互作用。即使你生来就有一组特定的基因，你的生活方式也会影响它们的表达方式。一些生活方式因素甚至可能打开或关闭基因。

paragraphs.sourceText: Deep within the genetic heart of all our cells are telomeres, or repeating segments of noncoding DNA that live at the ends of the chromosomes (染色体). They form caps at the ends of the chromosomes and keep the genetic material together. Shortening with each cell division, they help determine how fast a cell ages. When they become too short, the cell stops dividing altogether. This isn’t the only reason a cell can age — there are other stresses on cells we don’t yet understand very well — but short telomeres are one of the major reasons human cells grow old. We’ve devoted most of our careers to studying telomeres, and one extraordinary discovery from our labs is that telomeres can actually lengthen.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们所有细胞的遗传核心深处都有端粒，即位于染色体（染色体）末端的非编码 DNA 重复片段。它们在染色体末端形成帽子，并将遗传物质保持在一起。它们随着每次细胞分裂而缩短，有助于确定细胞衰老的速度。当它们变得太短时，细胞完全停止分裂。这并不是细胞衰老的唯一原因——我们还不太了解细胞面临的其他压力——但端粒短是人类细胞衰老的主要原因之一。我们的大部分职业生涯都致力于研究端粒，我们实验室的一项非凡发现是端粒实际上可以延长。

paragraphs.sourceText: Scientists have learned that several thought patterns appear to be unhealthy for telomeres, and one of them is cynical hostility. Cynical hostility is defined by high anger and frequent thoughts that other people cannot be trusted. Someone with hostility doesn’t just think, “I hate to stand in long lines”; they think, “Others deliberately sped up and beat me to my rightful position in the line!” — and then get violently agitated. People who score high on measures of cynical hostility tend to get more heart disease, metabolic disease and often die at younger ages. They also have shorter telomeres. In a study of British civil servants, men who scored high on measures of cynical hostility had shorter telomeres than men whose hostility scores were low. The most hostile men were 30% more likely to have short telomeres.
paragraphs.translationZh: 科学家们了解到，有几种思维模式似乎对端粒不健康，其中之一就是愤世嫉俗的敌意。愤世嫉俗的敌意是指高度愤怒和经常认为其他人不值得信任。怀有敌意的人不仅会想“我讨厌排长队”，还会想“我讨厌排长队”。他们想：“别人故意加快速度，把我抢到了队伍中应有的位置！” ——然后变得剧烈焦躁。在愤世嫉俗的敌意指标上得分较高的人往往会患更多的心脏病、代谢疾病，并且往往会在更年轻​​的时候死亡。它们的端粒也较短。在一项针对英国公务员的研究中，愤世嫉俗敌意得分高的男性比敌意得分低的男性端粒更短。最有敌意的男性端粒较短的可能性要高出 30%。

paragraphs.sourceText: What this means: aging is a dynamic process that could possibly be accelerated or slowed — and, in some aspects, even reversed. To an extent, it has surprised us and the rest of the scientific community that telomeres do not simply carry out the commands issued by your genetic code. Your telomeres are listening to you. The foods you eat, your response to challenges, the amount of exercise you get, and many other factors appear to influence your telomeres and can prevent premature aging at the cellular level. One of the keys to enjoying good health is simply doing your part to foster healthy cell renewal.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这意味着：衰老是一个动态过程，可能会加速或减慢，在某些方面甚至可能逆转。在某种程度上，端粒不仅仅执行遗传密码发出的命令，这让我们和科学界的其他人感到惊讶。你的端粒在听你说话。你吃的食物、你对挑战的反应、你的运动量以及许多其他因素似乎都会影响你的端粒，并可以在细胞水平上防止过早衰老。享受健康的关键之一就是尽自己的一份力量促进健康的细胞更新。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Scientists have created by accident an enzyme (酶) that breaks down plastic drinks bottles. The breakthrough could help solve the global plastic pollution crisis by enabling for the first time the full recycling of bottles.
paragraphs.translationZh: 科学家们偶然创造了一种可以分解塑料饮料瓶的酶。这一突破首次实现了瓶子的完全回收，有助于解决全球塑料污染危机。

paragraphs.sourceText: The new research was spurred by the discovery in 2016 of the first bacterium that had naturally evolved to eat plastic at a waste dump in Japan. Scientists have now revealed the detailed structure of the crucial enzyme produced by the bug.
paragraphs.translationZh: 2016 年，在日本的一个垃圾场发现了第一种自然进化来吃塑料的细菌，这推动了这项新研究。科学家们现在已经揭示了这种细菌产生的关键酶的详细结构。

paragraphs.sourceText: An international team then adjusted the enzyme to see how it had evolved, but tests showed they had accidentally made the molecule even better at breaking down the plastic used for drinks bottles. “What actually turned out was we improved the enzyme, which was a bit of a shock,” said head researcher Prof. McGeehan, at the University of Portsmouth, UK.
paragraphs.translationZh: 随后，一个国际团队对这种酶进行了调整，看看它是如何进化的，但测试表明，他们意外地使这种分子能够更好地分解用于饮料瓶的塑料。英国朴茨茅斯大学首席研究员麦吉汉教授说：“实际上，我们改进了酶，这有点令人震惊。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Currently, the enzyme takes a few days to start breaking down the plastic, far faster than the centuries it takes in the oceans, but the researchers are optimistic this can be speeded up even further and become a viable large-scale process.
paragraphs.translationZh: 目前，这种酶需要几天的时间才能开始分解塑料，这比在海洋中需要几个世纪的时间要快得多，但研究人员乐观地认为，这可以进一步加快，并成为一个可行的大规模过程。

paragraphs.sourceText: “What we are hoping to do is use this enzyme to turn this plastic back into its original components, so we can literally recycle it back to plastic,” said McGeehan. “It means we won’t need to dig up any more oil and, fundamentally, it should reduce the amount of plastic in the environment.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 麦吉汉说：“我们希望做的是使用这种酶将这种塑料变回其原始成分，这样我们就可以将其回收回塑料。” “这意味着我们不再需要开采更多的石油，而且从根本上说，它应该减少环境中的塑料量。”

paragraphs.sourceText: About 1 million plastic bottles are sold each minute around the globe and, with just 14% recycled, many end up in the oceans where they have polluted even the remotest parts, harming marine life and potentially people who eat seafood. “Plastic is incredibly resistant to degradation.” said McGeehan. “It is one of these wonder materials that has been made a little bit too well.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 全球每分钟售出约 100 万个塑料瓶，其中只有 14% 被回收利用，许多塑料瓶最终流入海洋，甚至污染了最偏远的地区，危害海洋生物，甚至可能危害吃海鲜的人们。 “塑料具有令人难以置信的抗降解能力。”麦吉汉说。 “这是一种制作得有点太好的神奇材料。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Currently those bottles that are recycled can only be turned into opaque fibres for clothing or carpets, while the new enzyme indicates a way to recycle old clear plastic bottles back into new clear plastic bottles.
paragraphs.translationZh: 目前，那些被回收的瓶子只能变成用于衣服或地毯的不透明纤维，而新的酶表明了一种将旧的透明塑料瓶回收成新的透明塑料瓶的方法。

paragraphs.sourceText: “You are always up against the fact that oil is cheap, so plastic is cheap,” said McGeehan. “It is so easy for manufacturers to generate more of that stuff, rather than even try to recycle, but I believe there is a public interest here: perception is changing so much that companies are starting to look at how they can properly recycle these bottles.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “你总是要面对这样一个事实：石油很便宜，所以塑料也很便宜，”麦吉汉说。 “制造商很容易生产更多这样的东西，甚至不需要尝试回收，但我相信这里有公众利益：观念正在发生巨大变化，以至于公司开始考虑如何正确回收这些瓶子。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Prof. Adisa Azapagic, at the University of Manchester in the UK, agreed the enzyme could be useful but added: “A full life-cycle assessment would be needed to ensure that the technology does not solve one environmental problem — waste — at the expense of others, including additional greenhouse gas emissions.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 英国曼彻斯特大学的 Adisa Azapagic 教授同意这种酶可能有用，但他补充道：“需要进行完整的生命周期评估，以确保该技术不会以牺牲其他环境问题（包括额外的温室气体排放）为代价来解决一个环境问题（废物）。”
